Desflurane is a volatile inhaled anaesthetic agent with:

- MAC 6
- Low blood:gas partition coefficient 0.42
- Low solubility oil:gas partition coefficient 29

These properties give Desflurane rapid washout even after long anaesthetic time due to low blood:gas and oil:gas partition coefficients.

Desflurane uptake/distribution can be modelled by the main distribution compartments, as solubility of Desflurane is so low its offset is almost duration independent. 

Washout of desflurane is dependent on establishing and maintaining a decreasing concentration gradient from compartment → blood → alveolus → circuit.  

Washout is a multi-exponential process graphed by FA/FA0 curve against time

![](/content/exams/anzca/2014/B/2/standard-image8.png){fig-alt="Desflurane washout curve showing distribution and terminal elimination phases"}

Phases:

1. Rapid washout of agent from Circuit and FRC

    - Circuit wash out dependant on FGF and circuit volume, t=CV/FGF
    - FRC washout dependant on MV and FRC volume t=FRC/MV

2. Washout from blood to alveolus:

    ↑CO → lower ΔP across alveolar membrane → slower washout

    ↓Blood:gas partition coefficient →↑ agent ΔP across alveolar membrane → Rapid washout

3. Washout form Compartments → Blood

    - Duration of Anaesthesia: ↑ Duration →↑uptake into body compartments → slower washout
    - Final end-tidal partial pressure of agent: ↑final concentration → increased tissue concentration → slower washout 
    - Very low O:G partition coefficient: Minimally soluble agents like desflurane so washout from compartments is relatively rapid
